beginner.summary: For web and back-end developers who are new to GraphQL. Covers how GraphQL differs from REST, the schema definition language, queries, arguments and fragments, mutations and input types, resolvers and execution, a first Apollo Server, database-backed resolvers, nullability and errors, enums, interfaces and unions, cursor pagination, client operations and variables, authentication and field authorisation, DataLoader, Apollo Client, subscriptions, testing, tooling and deployment.
prerequisites: Writes JavaScript or TypeScript and has used npm
Has built or called a REST API
outcomes: Design GraphQL schemas for real products
Build GraphQL servers with resolvers, pagination and auth
Call GraphQL APIs from web clients
Test, document and deploy a GraphQL API

days.topic: GraphQL Overview and Development Setup
subtopics: What GraphQL is and the problems it solves
One endpoint, typed schema and client-chosen fields
Installing Node.js and TypeScript for the course
GraphiQL and Apollo Sandbox for exploring APIs
How the course project is organised
Where GraphQL is used in industry
days.lab_task: Explore a public GraphQL API in GraphiQL, write queries that fetch exactly the fields a screen needs, compare the payload with the equivalent REST calls and set up the course project.
checks: Each query returns only the fields the screen needs
Request count and payload size compared
Types and fields found through introspection

days.topic: Schema Definition Language: Types, Fields and Scalars
subtopics: Descriptions and documentation in the schema
days.lab_task: Write the schema for a bookstore with books, authors, reviews and a DateTime scalar, document every type and field and validate it with graphql-js.
checks: Every type and field has a description

days.topic: Queries, Arguments, Aliases and Fragments
days.lab_task: Write queries against the course API that use arguments, nested selections, aliases to compare two books, named fragments shared by two screens and conditional fields with @include.
days.deliverable: Query library for the course API
checks: Two books fetched side by side in one query
@include adds and removes fields by variable
objectives: Shape responses with aliases and directives

days.topic: Mutations and Input Types
days.lab_task: Add createBook, updateBook, addReview and deleteReview mutations with input types and payload types that return changed data and user errors.
checks: Mutation returns the new book with its ID
Payload returns user errors without a server error
Mutations run in order in one request

days.topic: Resolvers and the Execution Model
subtopics: What a resolver receives: parent, args, context and info
Keeping business logic out of resolvers
days.lab_task: Implement resolvers for the bookstore schema with a per-request context, log the order resolvers run in for a nested query and move business rules into service modules.
days.deliverable: Resolver implementation with notes on execution
checks: Resolver order for a nested query explained
Request ID available in every resolver
Resolvers call services instead of holding rules

days.topic: Building a First Server with Apollo Server
days.lab_task: Run the bookstore API on Apollo Server inside Express, add a logging plugin, configure environments, disable the sandbox in production and shut down cleanly.
checks: Every operation name logged with timing

days.topic: Connecting Resolvers to a Database
subtopics: Choosing a data layer for GraphQL
Mapping database rows to GraphQL types
days.lab_task: Back the bookstore API with PostgreSQL through Prisma, map rows to types, implement filters from arguments and wrap review creation and rating updates in a transaction.
checks: Filters change the SQL that runs
Review and rating saved together or not at all

days.topic: Lists, Nullability and Error Handling
subtopics: The errors array and partial data
User errors in payloads compared with top-level errors
days.lab_task: Make nullability choices for the schema, show null propagation when a resolver fails, return coded errors, mask internal details in production and document the error policy.
checks: Partial data returned with an error entry

days.topic: Enums, Interfaces and Unions
days.lab_task: Add a Product interface for books and e-books, a search union across books, authors and series, enums for formats and resolve abstract types correctly.
checks: Union returns books, authors and series
Shared fields and type-specific fields both returned
objectives: Model with enums, interfaces and unions

days.topic: Pagination with Cursors and Connections
days.lab_task: Add cursor-based connections for books and reviews with forward and backward paging, filters and optional total counts, and test page boundaries.
checks: No duplicates or gaps across pages
hasNextPage correct on the last page

days.topic: Variables and Operation Names in Clients
subtopics: Required variables and type checking of inputs
days.lab_task: Call the API from a small web page with fetch using named operations and variables, show why string-building queries is unsafe and log operations by name on the server.
checks: Same operation reused with different variables
String-built query injection demonstrated and fixed

days.topic: Authentication in GraphQL Context
subtopics: Reading tokens or cookies into context
Signing in through a mutation or a separate endpoint
days.lab_task: Add JWT authentication that builds the current user in context, protect the addReview mutation, return a clear error for missing tokens and test authenticated operations.
checks: Mutation runs as the signed-in user
Tests cover signed-in and anonymous users

days.topic: Authorisation Rules on Fields
subtopics: Role checks with directives or middleware
Hiding fields compared with returning errors
Avoiding leaks through introspection and errors
days.lab_task: Protect fields so only authors see draft books and only admins see sales figures, enforce ownership on edits and test every role against every protected field.
checks: Every role and field combination tested

days.topic: The N+1 Problem and DataLoader
subtopics: How nested queries cause N+1 database calls
days.lab_task: Measure database queries for a nested books-with-authors-and-reviews query, add DataLoaders for each relation and show the query count drop.
days.deliverable: Loaders with before and after query counts
checks: N+1 pattern visible in the query log
Query count drops to one per relation
Missing IDs return null without errors

days.topic: Calling GraphQL from a Web Client with Apollo Client
days.lab_task: Build a small React page that lists and filters books with useQuery, adds reviews with useMutation, updates the list after a mutation and inspects the cache in devtools.
checks: List updates after the mutation without a full reload

days.topic: Subscriptions for Real-Time Updates
days.lab_task: Add a reviewAdded subscription filtered by book, publish events from the mutation, authenticate the WebSocket connection and show live reviews in the React page.
checks: Clients receive only their book's reviews

days.topic: Testing GraphQL APIs
subtopics: What to test in a GraphQL API
Executing operations in tests without HTTP
days.lab_task: Write tests that execute operations directly and over HTTP, cover errors and authorisation, snapshot the schema and run the suite in CI.
checks: Operation tests run without starting a server
Schema change fails the snapshot until reviewed

days.topic: Documenting and Exploring APIs with GraphiQL and Apollo Sandbox
days.lab_task: Add descriptions, deprecations and example operations to the API, publish a static documentation site from the schema and onboard a classmate as a new client developer.
checks: Every type and field documented on the site
Peer writes a working query from the docs alone

days.topic: Deploying a GraphQL Server
subtopics: Disabling introspection and sandbox where needed
tools: A cloud platform such as Render or Azure Container Apps
days.lab_task: Containerise the API with production settings and health checks, deploy it to a cloud platform with PostgreSQL, run smoke tests and confirm logging works.
days.deliverable: Live GraphQL API and deployment guide

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Bookstore GraphQL API
days.lab_task: Complete the bookstore API with a documented schema, mutations, pagination, authentication and field rules, DataLoaders, subscriptions, a React client, tests and a deployment, then demo it.
days.deliverable: Repository, live API, client and demo recording
checks: Queries, mutations and live reviews work end to end
objectives: Combine the beginner topics in one API

intermediate.summary: For developers who already build GraphQL APIs. Covers schema design for products, code-first servers with Pothos and GraphQL Yoga, type generation, errors as data, advanced pagination and filtering, caching and persisted queries, the Apollo Client cache, Relay conventions, uploads, security limits, resolver performance, schema evolution, custom directives, subscriptions at scale, gateways over services, testing strategy, observability, GraphQL in other languages and schema checks in CI.
prerequisites: Has built a GraphQL API with resolvers, mutations and authentication
outcomes: Build typed, secure and fast GraphQL servers
Cache and evolve GraphQL APIs safely
Run GraphQL across services and languages

days.topic: Schema Design Principles for Product APIs
days.lab_task: Redesign a database-shaped schema from client use cases, apply naming and nullability rules, model intent-based mutations and run a schema review with a checklist.
checks: Each client screen served by the new schema

days.topic: Code-First Servers with Pothos and GraphQL Yoga
subtopics: Pothos plugins for auth, errors and Prisma
Choosing an approach for a team
days.lab_task: Rebuild part of the API code-first with Pothos and the Prisma plugin on GraphQL Yoga, add the auth and errors plugins and compare type safety with the SDL version.
checks: TypeScript catches a resolver returning the wrong shape

days.topic: Type Generation with GraphQL Code Generator
subtopics: Keeping generated code out of reviews
days.lab_task: Generate resolver types for the server and typed documents with fragment masking for the React client, run generation in watch mode and fail CI when generated code is stale.
checks: Type errors appear in affected client components
Components read only their own fragment fields
Stale generated code fails the build

days.topic: Errors as Data: Result Types and Error Unions
subtopics: Combining with top-level errors for system failures
days.lab_task: Convert checkout and review mutations to result unions with typed errors, handle each error type in the client and keep system failures as top-level errors.
checks: Client receives a typed error object
Each error type shows a specific message
Top-level error returned with a code

days.topic: Advanced Pagination, Filtering and Sorting
subtopics: Combining filters with AND and OR
days.lab_task: Design filter and sort inputs for the catalogue, implement keyset pagination that stays stable under sorting, cap page sizes and check query plans.
checks: Pages stay consistent when sorting by price

days.topic: Caching: HTTP, Persisted Queries and Response Caches
days.lab_task: Add automatic persisted queries, serve public queries over GET through a CDN with cache hints, cache responses on the server and keep private data out of shared caches.
checks: Repeat requests send only the query hash
Public query served from the CDN

days.topic: Apollo Client Cache: Normalisation, Policies and Updates
days.lab_task: Configure type and field policies for paginated lists, update the cache after mutations without refetching, add optimistic responses and fix a stale-data bug.
checks: Mutation updates the list from the cache
Cause of the stale list identified and fixed

days.topic: Relay Conventions: Global IDs, Connections and Fragments
subtopics: Global object identification and the node field
Mutations and store updates in Relay
days.lab_task: Make the server Relay-compatible with global IDs and the node field, build a Relay page with colocated fragments and compare the developer experience with Apollo Client.
checks: Any object refetched through the node field
Each component declares its own data
Trade-offs of Relay and Apollo recorded

days.topic: File Uploads and Large Payloads in GraphQL
subtopics: The multipart request specification and its risks
days.lab_task: Implement uploads through signed URLs requested by a mutation, record upload status, compare with multipart uploads and add size limits and CSRF protection.
days.deliverable: Upload flow with notes on trade-offs
checks: File goes straight to storage through a signed URL

days.topic: Security: Depth Limits, Cost Analysis and Introspection Control
subtopics: Denial of service through deep or wide queries
days.lab_task: Attack the API with deep, wide and aliased queries, add depth, cost and alias limits, rate-limit by cost, restrict introspection and retest with a GraphQL security scanner.
checks: Query rejected by the depth limit

days.topic: Performance: Tracing Resolvers and Batching
tools: Apollo usage reporting or GraphQL Hive
days.lab_task: Trace a slow operation to its resolvers, use look-ahead to fetch only requested columns, batch an external API call, cache a hot resolver and prove the gains under load.
checks: Slowest resolver identified in the trace
p95 latency lower after the changes

days.topic: Schema Evolution and Deprecation
subtopics: Breaking changes and how to avoid them
days.lab_task: Deprecate and replace two fields, track usage until clients move, detect breaking changes with GraphQL Inspector and remove a field only when usage reaches zero.
checks: Usage of the deprecated field reported per client
Field removed only after zero usage

days.topic: Directives: Built-In and Custom
days.lab_task: Implement a @formatDate directive and an @auth directive with schema transforms, compare them with plugin-based approaches and document both.

days.topic: Subscriptions at Scale with WebSockets and Server-Sent Events
subtopics: Scaling with Redis or other pub/sub
days.lab_task: Scale subscriptions across three instances with Redis pub/sub, switch a client to SSE, handle slow consumers and load test 5,000 concurrent subscribers.
days.deliverable: Scaled subscription setup with test results
checks: Events reach subscribers on all instances
5,000 subscribers served at the target latency

days.topic: GraphQL over Microservices: Schema Stitching and Gateways
subtopics: Exposing many services through one graph
Gateways in front of REST services
Error and timeout handling across services
days.lab_task: Build one graph over a REST product service and a GraphQL review service with GraphQL Mesh and stitching, propagate auth and handle a slow downstream service.
checks: One operation returns data from both services
Downstream services receive the user identity
Gateway times out and returns partial data

days.topic: Testing Strategy: Unit, Integration and Contract Tests for Schemas
subtopics: Schema checks against real client operations
days.lab_task: Build a layered test suite with resolver tests, container-backed integration tests, mocked-schema client tests and operation checks that block changes breaking known client queries.
checks: Tests pass against a real PostgreSQL container
Breaking change caught against saved operations
Client tests run without a server

days.topic: Observability for GraphQL APIs
subtopics: Why HTTP metrics are not enough
Error rates by operation and field
days.lab_task: Instrument the API for operation and resolver telemetry, identify clients by name and version, build dashboards for slow and failing operations and alert on error spikes.
checks: Trace shows resolver spans and database calls
Metrics split by client name and version
Alert fires for an error spike on one operation

days.topic: GraphQL in Other Languages: Strawberry, Hot Chocolate, gqlgen and Spring for GraphQL
subtopics: The same schema in several languages
Batching and auth in each ecosystem
days.lab_task: Implement the same small schema in two other languages, run the same client operations against all three servers and compare batching, auth and developer experience.
days.deliverable: Two extra implementations and a comparison
checks: All servers return the same results
Batching approach documented for each stack
Recommendation for a given team context
objectives: Build GraphQL servers in other languages

days.topic: CI/CD and Schema Checks
days.lab_task: Build a pipeline that lints the schema, checks changes against recorded client operations, publishes the schema, deploys the server and rolls back a bad release.
checks: Pipeline blocks a change that breaks a live client
Registry shows the new schema version

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Typed GraphQL API for a Marketplace
days.lab_task: Build a marketplace API with a reviewed schema, code-first server, generated types, result-type errors, keyset pagination, caching, security limits, subscriptions, observability and schema checks in CI, then present it.
days.deliverable: Repository, live API, reports and presentation
checks: Listing, buying and live updates work end to end
Security, performance and test reports meet targets
Schema choices explained against client use cases
objectives: Combine the intermediate topics in one API

advanced.summary: For senior API engineers and platform teams running GraphQL at scale. Covers execution internals, Apollo Federation v2, subgraph and entity design, supergraph routing, schema governance, persisted operations and abuse protection, query planning, caching at scale, live queries and incremental delivery, mobile clients, REST migration, GraphQL as a BFF, data access patterns, multi-tenancy, observability and SLOs, testing federated graphs, GraphQL for AI agents, platform operating models and incident troubleshooting.
prerequisites: Several years building production GraphQL APIs
Strong TypeScript or another server language
outcomes: Architect federated supergraphs for many teams
Engineer performance, caching and security at scale
Govern schemas and migrations across an organisation
Lead GraphQL platform decisions and incident response

days.topic: GraphQL Execution Internals: Parsing, Validation and Execution
days.lab_task: Parse documents and walk the AST, write a custom validation rule that blocks a field pattern, step through execution in the debugger and explain null propagation from the source.
days.deliverable: Internals notebook with a custom rule
checks: Visitor reports every field in a document
Null propagation explained from the source code

days.topic: Federation Architecture with Apollo Federation v2
days.lab_task: Split the marketplace graph into products, reviews and users subgraphs, compose a supergraph, move a field between subgraphs with @override and fix composition errors.
checks: Product query returns fields from all three subgraphs
Field moved with @override without client changes

days.topic: Subgraph Design and Entity Ownership
subtopics: Mapping subgraphs to teams and domains
days.lab_task: Design subgraph boundaries for a retailer with four teams, batch reference resolvers, remove a chatty entity pattern and run a cross-team design review.
checks: Fewer subgraph calls for the key operation

days.topic: Supergraph Routing with Apollo Router or Hive Gateway
subtopics: Header propagation and auth at the router
days.lab_task: Run the supergraph behind a router with JWT checks, header propagation, a coprocessor for custom policy, timeouts per subgraph and telemetry, then scale it to three replicas.
checks: Unauthenticated operations stopped at the router
Slow subgraph returns a partial response within the limit
Plan for the main operation explained

days.topic: Schema Governance for Many Teams
days.lab_task: Set up a schema registry with ownership metadata, lint rules, contracts for a partner variant and an approval workflow, then process two changes from different teams.
checks: Partner variant exposes only approved fields
Change approved by the owning team before publish

days.topic: Advanced Security: Persisted Operations, Rate Limits and Abuse Protection
subtopics: Trusted documents and persisted operation lists
Rate limits by client and cost
Batching and alias abuse at scale
days.lab_task: Move first-party clients to trusted documents, block arbitrary operations, apply cost-based limits per client, detect abuse in logs and run a penetration test.
checks: Router rejects operations not on the list

days.topic: Query Planning and Performance at Scale
days.lab_task: Analyse query plans for the top five operations, cut subgraph fetches with @provides, defer slow fields, load test the supergraph and set budgets per operation.
checks: Fewer subgraph calls in the new plan
Initial response arrives before the slow field
Budgets met for the top operations

days.topic: Caching Strategies at Scale: CDN, Entity Caching and Invalidation
tools: Apollo Router entity caching or Hive response cache
days.lab_task: Add entity caching and CDN caching for public operations, invalidate by entity when products change, keep personalised fields uncached and measure hit rates and freshness.
checks: Updated product appears within the freshness target
Public operations served from the CDN

days.topic: Real-Time Architectures: Subscriptions, Live Queries and Incremental Delivery
days.lab_task: Add federated subscriptions fed from Kafka, stream a long list with @stream, defer slow fields and compare the cost and complexity of each approach.
checks: Events from a subgraph reach clients through the router
Cost and complexity recorded for each
objectives: Build real-time features in federated graphs

days.topic: GraphQL for Mobile Clients: Offline, Persisted Queries and Versioning
subtopics: Mobile constraints: network, battery and release cycles
days.lab_task: Ship a mobile client with persisted queries and an offline cache, track usage by app version and plan field removal while old versions are still in use.
days.deliverable: Mobile client setup and deprecation plan
checks: Cached data shown without a connection
Field removal timed to app version usage

days.topic: Migrating REST APIs to GraphQL
subtopics: Reasons to migrate and reasons not to
Wrapping REST endpoints as a first step
Running REST and GraphQL side by side
tools: Apollo Connectors or REST data sources
days.lab_task: Wrap three REST services in the graph, move one into a native subgraph, migrate a client screen, track adoption and retire one REST endpoint safely.
checks: REST data available in the graph

days.topic: GraphQL as a Backend for Frontend
subtopics: One graph or one BFF per client
days.lab_task: Build a GraphQL BFF for a mobile app over existing services, compare it with a shared supergraph, enforce screen performance budgets and decide ownership.
checks: One operation serves the whole home screen
Screen operation within its latency budget
objectives: Compare BFF and shared graph designs

days.topic: Data Access Patterns: Databases, Search and Third-Party APIs Behind GraphQL
subtopics: Resolving from SQL and NoSQL stores
days.lab_task: Serve one product type from PostgreSQL, search results from OpenSearch and stock from a rate-limited third-party API, batch and cache across sources and handle partial failures.
checks: Third-party calls stay under the limit
Partial data returned with a clear error

days.topic: Multi-Tenant GraphQL APIs
subtopics: Tenant context at the router and subgraphs
days.lab_task: Make the marketplace graph multi-tenant with tenant context from tokens, row-level security, per-tenant limits and a schema variant for premium tenants, and prove isolation.
checks: No cross-tenant data in any operation
Premium fields visible only to premium tenants

days.topic: Observability and SLOs for Supergraphs
subtopics: Tracing across the router and subgraphs
Dashboards for platform and product teams
days.lab_task: Trace operations across router and subgraphs, define SLOs for the checkout and search operations, alert on burn rate and build dashboards for the platform team.
checks: One trace covers router and all subgraphs
Alert fires during a simulated failure
Dashboards show health per operation and client

days.topic: Testing Federated Graphs
days.lab_task: Build a test strategy for the supergraph with isolated subgraph tests, composition checks, operation contracts, router end-to-end tests and query plan performance tests.
checks: Key operations pass through the router
Plan regressions caught by performance tests

days.topic: GraphQL and AI: Agents and LLM Tool Calling over a Graph
subtopics: Why a graph suits AI agents
Model Context Protocol servers over GraphQL
Cost and rate limits for agent traffic
days.lab_task: Expose a curated set of graph operations as tools through an MCP server, let an agent answer catalogue questions, restrict it to safe operations and audit its usage.
checks: Agent answers questions through approved operations
Agent cannot run operations outside its list
objectives: Connect AI agents to a graph

days.topic: Platform Team Operating Model for GraphQL
days.lab_task: Define the operating model for a GraphQL platform team, publish a subgraph template and golden path, set adoption metrics and present a roadmap.
checks: New subgraph created and composed in a day

days.topic: Troubleshooting Production GraphQL Incidents
days.lab_task: Work through four incidents: a plan regression, a subgraph outage, an abusive client and a client cache bug, restore service and write one post-incident review.
days.deliverable: Incident notes and a post-incident review
checks: All four incidents mitigated within their time limits
Each cause backed by traces or registry history
Review lists causes and follow-up actions

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Federated Supergraph for a Retail Platform
days.lab_task: Design and build a federated supergraph for a retailer with four subgraphs, router policy, trusted documents, entity caching, real-time features, governance workflows and SLOs, then defend it to a review panel.
days.deliverable: Supergraph repository, governance pack and defence
checks: Load test meets the agreed SLOs
Breaking changes blocked by the workflow
Review panel questions answered with evidence
objectives: Combine the advanced topics in one platform
